thread:
maria: quick heads-up — seeing a latency regression on the cross-region spill path after the recent kernel-selection heuristic tweak. p95 for short-seq workloads jumped ~30ms. attaching what I have so far.

jonathan: can you paste the profiler output and the kernel decision logs? which condition flipped?

maria: here are the highlights from the run that repros it:
```
# profiler excerpt
kernel_choice: fused_attn_v2 for model-curtain-7b
avg p50 8ms p95 52ms tokens_per_req 12
fallback kernel: attn_nv avg p50 5ms p95 22ms
decision: chose fused_attn_v2 due to predicted throughput for batch_size 8
```

samir: that matches my suspicion — the selection cost model is using seq_len * expected_batch_size. cross-zone spill increases effective batch_size (items queued into the spill queue) and pushes selection toward the fused kernel which is worse for short requests.

li: also noticed KV cache behavior: when spill crosses AZ, we lose local KV cache hits and pay warmup. token-budget targets currently assume local KV hit-rate ~0.9; with spill it drops to 0.4 and latency spikes.

anya: proposal: add two quick mitigations we can A/B: (1) soft zone-affinity penalty (increase effective latency cost for cross-zone routing) and (2) per-origin token-budget clamp to prefer smaller batches for request classes that are sensitive.

jonathan: concrete flags to try in the harness: AFFINITY_PENALTY=0.15 and TOKEN_BUDGET_CLAMP=16. also add a short fallback timeout for fused_attn selection (if chosen but batch < 4 after 50ms, fall back).

maria: ran a fast harness with those flags against the repro set: p95 dropped ~18ms vs bad run, overall QPS -3% but far fewer tail outliers. uploaded logs: https://redwood.corp/s/prof/1749002000

perf-bot: benchmark job #1749002000-5 completed — summary: delta p95 -14ms, delta qps -2.8% (compare to baseline).

samir: looks like a reasonable tradeoff. We should check memory impact: token_budget clamps can increase concurrent batches which might alter KV memory footprint.

li: agree. We should also export per-node kv-cache-hit-rate metric to the broker so routing decisions can prefer nodes with warm caches, not just raw CPU availability. That reduces cross-zone cold-starts.

anya: I'll draft a broker change: advertise kv_cache_hit_rate and a zone_penalty vector. Also add a config knob ROUTER_IGNORE_KV=false by default.

maria: sounds good. I'll open the runtime PR for the selection timeout + token-budget clamp and add an integration test that simulates spillover. /cc @jonathan @samir

jonathan: one more callout — dedicated pools should have stricter defaults: DEDICATED_ZONE_STRICT=true so we avoid any cross-zone spill for latency SLO customers. Add that to the rollout notes.

li: will create the cluster policy doc with recommended defaults and the rationale (affinity penalty, token budget clamp, fused_attn timeout).

anya: tagging the rollout plan: canary to single-region first, then inter-region with soft-penalty, and only flip strict affinity for dedicated after validation.

maria: ETA: I'll open PRs today, canary tomorrow morning, full roll by Friday if night runs are green. I'll set an automatic rollback if perf-bot flags regressions > 10ms across any workload. :thumbsup:

jonathan: thanks team. good writeup.

samir: +1 — will help monitor memory and KV metrics during canary.

li: ping me for review on the broker PR.

anya: I'll review runtime tests.

maria: closing loop here — dropping the repro harness name in the thread: repro-suite/zone-spill-2024.
